text:
Sophie (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining the Q&A thread after today's all-hands. Quick summary from leadership: we're moving forward with a targeted headcount plan over the next 12 months to support Dedicated, Private, and runtime performance work. High-level add: 36 new roles across Eng/Product/DevEx/Support — details below, ask questions here and we'll follow up with docs.

Andre (People Ops): Timeline and mechanics — hiring starts immediately. We're phasing hires in three waves: Q2 (~12 hires), Q3 (~14), Q4 (~10). Internal transfers get priority for lateral moves; relocation and visa support handled case-by-case.

Liam (Product): One clarification: most product hires are PMs for Dedicated and Private features and a small growth PM for self-serve. We won't open core infra PMs until Q3 to avoid overlapping interviews.

Ravi (Eng Manager): Quick Q: how are the 18 Eng slots broken down? Any reserved hires for runtime vs infra vs ML?

Marta (VP Eng): Eng split: runtime 7, infra 5, eng-ml 3, sres/oncall 3. We plan ~40% senior hires (senior/staff+) to accelerate ownership. A subset of runtime hires will be focused on quantization and low-latency kernels.

Theo (Staff SWE): For folks wanting to transfer in: what's the internal timeline for interviews and does comp get re-banded?

Andre (People Ops): Internal mobility flow: 2-week expression-of-interest window, internal interview window ~4 weeks. Offers aim to align with existing market bands; we try to keep comp neutral but approvals for above-band moves will need exec sign-off. DM me for edge cases.

Ava (Recruiter): Hiring process for ICs: 1) quick screen 2) small take-home or design exercise 3) on-site loop. For runtime roles we emphasize system design + kernel/latency questions. Internal candidates often get a shortened loop when qualifications match. Link to openings will go live after internal notif.

Theo (Staff SWE): Any planned changes to oncall? Runtime folks are worried about being overloaded during rollouts.

Marta (VP Eng): Yes — we're rebalancing oncall by introducing a squad-level "resilience" owner and shifting some ops responsibilities into Dedicated on-call rotations. Expected reduction of peak oncall load ~20% after hires and runbook work.

Ravi (Eng Manager): How will this affect team boundaries? Will teams be merged or split?

Sophie (CEO): No mass merges planned; we will do targeted reorganizations where they drive clearer ownership (e.g., separate "Serving Runtime" vs "Serving Orchestration" squads). Managers will get proposed org diagrams this week; team-specific changes will be consultative.

ProductBot: Internal reference — headcount spreadsheet and interactive org map are posted here: https://redwood.example.com/internal/headcount-plan and https://redwood.example.com/internal/org-map

Andre (People Ops): Action items from this thread: 1) publish the detailed headcount spreadsheet (EOD) 2) open internal transfers form (link in doc) 3) schedule manager syncs to review proposed team shifts.

Sophie (CEO): Thanks for the questions — please keep them coming. If you have manager- or payroll-specific concerns, @Andre (People Ops) is the go-to. We'll follow up with an FAQ and timeline. :thumbsup:
